shortDescription: VANCOUVER, BC / ACCESS Newswire / October 5, 2026 / Hillcrest Energy Technologies Ltd. children: ("Hillcrest" or the "Company") today provided shareholders with an update on negotiations toward a definitive agreement with Equipmake plc ("Equipmake") for Hillcrest's Zero Voltage Switching ("ZVS") inverter technology. The scope of the agreement under negotiation has expanded beyond joint development to include commercial licensing terms. The Company expects to complete the agreement in October 2026.

On July 9, 2026, Hillcrest announced a non-binding Letter of Intent ("LOI") with Equipmake, a UK-based developer and manufacturer of high-performance electric motors and inverters. The LOI set out a joint development program to integrate Hillcrest's proprietary ZVS technology into a defined Equipmake powertrain product line. The parties agreed to use commercially reasonable efforts to execute a definitive agreement within 90 days of the LOI date.

Since the LOI was signed, the scope of the proposed agreement has expanded. The LOI contemplated negotiating licensing terms at a later stage. The parties are now negotiating a single definitive agreement that would cover both the joint development program and the commercial licensing terms for the resulting product. Addressing commercialization now is intended to give both companies a defined path from development to market.

Negotiations are advancing, and the Company expects to complete the definitive agreement in October 2026. This timeline extends modestly beyond the original 90-day target to reflect the expanded scope of the agreement. The terms of the agreement remain subject to negotiation and have not been finalized. There is no assurance that a definitive agreement will be executed within the anticipated timeframe, on the terms described in this news release. Hillcrest will announce the material terms of the agreement if and when it is executed.

"When we signed the LOI, the focus was on a joint development program. As our discussions with Equipmake progressed, both companies saw the value in agreeing now on the commercial terms that would follow successful development, rather than leaving them for a later negotiation," said Don Currie, CEO of Hillcrest. "That is a meaningful step up in scope, and it is the right structure for a long-term partnership. We are taking the time needed to get it right, and we expect to complete the agreement in October."

"Hillcrest's ZVS technology has characteristics we believe could take the performance of our inverters to the next level for our customers," said Ian Foley, Founder and CEO of Equipmake. "As our discussions progressed, it made sense to set out the commercial framework alongside the development program, so there is a clear route from engineering to market if the program succeeds. We are making good progress and look forward to completing the agreement with Hillcrest."

Hillcrest Energy Technologies Ltd. is a Canadian clean technology company developing advanced power conversion technologies and digital control systems for next-generation energy applications, including AI data centres, energy storage, industrial motor drives, microgrids, and electric-vehicle powertrains. The PCS1000 is Hillcrest's newest product platform, currently in the A-Sample prototype stage. For more information: https://hillcrestenergy.tech/
